Briefing for 18 November 2026

Short items for 18 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

New model

OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and the cheaper Sol

OpenAI's new frontier model Astra and the everyday model Sol are rolling out in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API. Astra's API prices drop 20 percent, cached input 60 percent.

Source: OpenAI

Everyday tool

AI Studio now builds full-stack Android apps

Google AI Studio can now set up a Firestore database, Google sign-in and secure Gemini API calls for Android apps from a prompt, and publish them to your personal Play library.

Source: Google Developers Blog

Everyday tool

Gemini's task mode is now free in six countries

Google is rolling out tasks in the Gemini app at no cost in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India, so it can work through chores instead of only answering. The EU is excluded.

Source: Google

AI agents

Devin Bots take on whole engineering goals

Cognition's new Devin Bots are persistent agents with their own memory that split a larger goal into tasks and run several Devin sessions in parallel. They bring only decisions back to people.

Source: Cognition

In the background

NATO uses OpenAI models for cyber defense

Through its Daybreak program, OpenAI gives NATO's communications agency access to advanced security models for finding vulnerabilities and testing fixes. NATO has used up to 300 billion tokens a month.

Source: OpenAI

In the background

Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion for AI drug design

The Google DeepMind spinout raised a $5 billion Series C co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia, with Alphabet investing again. The money goes into its drug design engine and its pipeline of candidates.

Source: Isomorphic Labs

Device

Genesis AI raises $500 million for dexterous robots

The robotics startup raised a $500 million Series A at a $3.5 billion valuation. It wants to bring robots with human-like hand skills into factories and warehouses.

Source: TechCrunch

In the background

EU science advisors warn against weaker AI rules

Two advisory groups of the European Commission call for keeping existing AI laws strong and for independent EU capacity to evaluate models instead of leaving that to developers.

Source: European Commission

Be brave. Get smart.
